item.title: Theories of Family Business Research
item.content:encoded:
This special issue invites scholarly contributions that advance theoretical understanding of family business phenomena. The issue seeks to explore how established theories from organizational science, management, and related disciplines can be adapted, extended, or challenged through family business research.

Contributions should critically examine existing theoretical frameworks and their applicability to family business contexts, or propose novel theoretical perspectives that enhance our understanding of how family dynamics, ownership structures, and generational transitions shape business behavior and outcomes.

Potential topics

  • Institutional theory and family business
  • Resource-based view in family business contexts
  • Stakeholder theory applications in family firms
  • Agency theory and family business governance
  • Stewardship theory in family business
  • Behavioral theories of family business decision-making
  • Social capital theory in family business
  • Organizational identity and family business
  • Dynamic capabilities in family business
  • Evolutionary perspectives on family business
  • Network theory and family business ecosystems
  • Psychological ownership in family contexts

item.title: Modern Family Firms
item.content:encoded: Family Business Review (FBR) is calling for papers for a special issue on Modern Family Firms. This special issue aims to explore contemporary issues, challenges, and opportunities facing family businesses in the modern era.
